\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Duality}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.General.Duality
\section{Overview}
The noise kernel has total mass one in either variable and contracts each norm of exponent at least one. Self-adjointness yields conjugate operator bounds and the hypercontractive estimate crossing exponent two.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Noise kernel rows sum to one]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_right}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign}
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_right}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0\le\rho\le1$, and fix $x\in\{0,1\}^n$.
The noise kernel
$K_\rho(x,y)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1+\rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2}$,
where $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$, satisfies
\[
  \sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^n}K_\rho(x,y)=1.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise kernel sums to one over the cube]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_left}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_right}
\difficulty{3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_left}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0\le\rho\le1$, and fix $y\in\{0,1\}^n$.
The noise kernel
$K_\rho(x,y)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1+\rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2}$,
where $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$, satisfies
\[
  \sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}K_\rho(x,y)=1.
\]
Thus $K_\rho(\cdot,y)$ is a probability distribution on the cube.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Jensen bound for powers of the noise operator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_abs_rpow_le_kernel_avg}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_right, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_eq_kernel_sum, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_abs_rpow_le_kernel_avg}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $T_\rho$ denote the noise operator with parameter
$\rho \in [0,1]$ acting on Boolean functions $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$. Then for every
real exponent $s \ge 1$ and every point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$,
\[
  \abs{(T_\rho f)(x)}^{s} \;\le\; \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^n} K_\rho(x,y)\,\abs{f(y)}^{s},
\]
where $K_\rho(x,y) = \prod_{i} \tfrac{1 + \rho\,\sigma(x_i)\,\sigma(y_i)}{2}$ is the
noise kernel, with $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Contractivity of the noise operator in $L^s$]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.trivial_contractivity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_left, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_abs_rpow_le_kernel_avg, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.trivial_contractivity}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $s \ge 1$ and $\rho \in [0,1]$, and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean
function. Then, with expectations taken under the uniform measure on the cube, the noise
operator $T_\rho$ satisfies
\[
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{T_\rho f}^{s}\bigr]\bigr)^{1/s}
  \;\le\;
  \bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{f}^{s}\bigr]\bigr)^{1/s}.
\] For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}

  {BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_ineq_bool}
  {direct}
  {boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}
  {pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p016-b006}
Fix a natural number $n$, exponents $p,q>1$ and a noise parameter $\rho$ with $0 \le \rho \le 1$, and write
$p' = p/(p-1)$ and $q' = q/(q-1)$ for the H\"older conjugates. Then the noise operator
$T_\rho$ on Boolean functions $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ satisfies the $(p \to q)$ bound
\[
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{T_\rho f}^q\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/q} \;\le\;
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^p\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p}
  \qquad \text{for every } f
\]
if and only if it satisfies the conjugate $(q' \to p')$ bound
\[
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{T_\rho f}^{p'}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p'} \;\le\;
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^{q'}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/q'}
  \qquad \text{for every } f,
\]
where all norms are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Square root of a ratio bounded by one]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Interpolation.sqrt_div_le_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Interpolation.sqrt_div_le_one}
Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers with $0 \le a$, $0 < b$, and $a \le b$. Then $\sqrt{a/b}
\le 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise-parameter identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_param_eq}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_param_eq}
Let $p, u \in \bbr$ with $u > 1$. Then
\[
  \Bigl(\frac{u}{u-1} - 1\Bigr)(p-1) \;=\; \frac{p-1}{u-1}.
\]
\end{lemma}

Fix a natural number $n$. Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, and let $p,u\in\bbr$ satisfy $1\le p\le
2\le u$. Set $\rho=\sqrt{(p-1)/(u-1)}$ and let $T_\rho$ denote the noise operator with

  \bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{T_\rho f}^{\,u}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/u}

  \bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^{\,p}\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p},
\]
where the expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Interpolation parameters for the low-norms case]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.low_norms_interpolation_params}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.low_norms_interpolation_params}
Let $p, u, \rho$ be real numbers with $1 < p < u < 2$, and suppose $\rho^2 =
(p-1)/(u-1)$. Then there exist real numbers $\theta \in (0,1)$ and $s > 0$ such that
\[
  \frac{1}{p} = \frac{\theta}{1+\rho^2} + \frac{1-\theta}{s}
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \frac{1}{u} = \frac{\theta}{2} + \frac{1-\theta}{s}.
\]
\end{lemma}
